# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

menu "C Library"

source "lib/libc/minimal/Kconfig"
source "lib/libc/picolibc/Kconfig"
source "lib/libc/newlib/Kconfig"

choice
	prompt "C library"
	default MINIMAL_LIBC
	help
	  Select the C library implementation to use.

config MINIMAL_LIBC
	bool "Minimal C library"
	select LIBC_MINIMAL
	help
	  This option enables the minimal C library. This library
	  provides a basic set of C library APIs.

config PICOLIBC
	bool "Picolibc C library"
	select PICOLIBC_SUPPORT
	select SYS_LIBC_HAS_REENT
	help
	  This option enables the Picolibc C library.

config NEWLIB_LIBC
	bool "Newlib C library"
	select NEWLIB_LIBC_SUPPORT
	select SYS_LIBC_HAS_REENT
	help
	  This option enables the Newlib C library.

config EXTERNAL_LIBC
	bool "External C library"
	help
	  This option indicates that an external C library is used.
	  This is automatically selected by toolchains that provide
	  their own C library.

endchoice

config LIBC_MINIMAL
	bool

config PICOLIBC_SUPPORT
	bool

config NEWLIB_LIBC_SUPPORT
	bool

config HAS_LIBC_PLUSPLUS
	bool "C++ library"
	depends on CPLUSPLUS
	help
	  Enable C++ support.

config CPLUSPLUS
	bool

config SYS_LIBC_HAS_REENT
	bool

config MALLOC_ALIGNMENT
	int
	default 8 if 64BIT
	default 4

config STACK_CANARIES
	bool "Compiler stack canaries"
	depends on TOOLCHAIN_HAS_STACK_CANARIES
	help
	  Enable compiler-generated stack canaries to detect stack
	  overflows. When a stack overflow is detected, the kernel
	  will treat it as a fatal error.

config LIBC_ERRNO
	bool "Use libc's errno"
	default y if NEWLIB_LIBC || PICOLIBC
	help
	  Use the C library's errno implementation instead of Zephyr's
	  thread-local implementation. This is required for C libraries
	  that are re-entrant.

config PRINTK
	bool "Enable printk"
	default y
	help
	  This option enables the printk() API, which is a non-standard
	  and simplified version of the standard printf() function.
	  It is used to print formatted strings to the console.

config EARLY_CONSOLE
	bool "Enable early console"
	depends on PRINTK
	help
	  Enable console before kernel is fully initialized.

config STDOUT_CONSOLE
	bool "Redirect stdout to console"
	default y if !(NATIVE_LIBRARY && EXTERNAL_LIBC)
	depends on CONSOLE
	depends on !(NATIVE_LIBRARY && EXTERNAL_LIBC)
	help
	  Redirect stdout to the console device. This makes functions
	  like printf() output to the system console.

endmenu

# Kconfig - fcb configuration options
#
# Copyright (c) 2017 Nordic Semiconductor ASA
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#

menuconfig FCB
	bool "Flash Circular Buffer"
	depends on FLASH
	help
	  Flash Circular Buffer (FCB) is a subsystem for managing data in
	  a circular buffer on flash memory.

if FCB

config FCB_CRC8
	bool "Enable CRC8 checksums for FCB entries"
	select CRC
	default y
	help
	  Enable CRC8 checksums for each entry in the FCB. This adds a
	  small overhead but provides data integrity checks.

config FCB_MAX_SECTORS
	int "Maximum number of sectors FCB can use"
	default 16
	help
	  Maximum number of sectors FCB can use. This determines the size of
	  the fcb->f_sectors array.

endif # FCB

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

# Common architecture-independent Kconfig options

# This file is included from the top-level Kconfig file.

config 64BIT
	bool
	help
	  Indicates that the architecture is 64-bit. The toolchain will
	  be selected based on this.

config STACK_POINTER_SHIFT
	int
	default 0
	help
	  If the stack pointer is not aligned to a word boundary, this is the
	  number of bits to shift it to the right to get the word-aligned
	  stack pointer.

config HAS_IMMEDIATE_IRQS
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a way to deliver
	  interrupts immediately, without going through the normal interrupt
	  handling path.

config ARCH_HAS_USERSPACE
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture supports user mode.

config ARCH_HAS_MMU_PT_PD_SIZE
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a way to specify
	  the size of the page table and page directory.

config CPU_HAS_MMU_FLAG_SUPPORT
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the CPU has hardware support for memory
	  management unit flags.

config ARCH_HAS_STACK_PROTECTION
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture supports stack
	  protection.

config ARCH_HAS_THREAD_ABORT
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture supports thread
	  abortion.

config ARCH_HAS_RAMFUNC_SUPPORT
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture supports placing
	  functions in RAM.

config ARCH_HAS_NESTED_EXCEPTION_DETECTION
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a way to detect
	  nested exceptions.

config ARCH_HAS_GDBSTUB
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has GDB stub support.

config ARCH_HAS_CPU_IDLE
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a CPU idle

config ARCH_HAS_NANO_TIMEOUT
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a nano-second
	  resolution timeout implementation.

config ARCH_HAS_COVERAGE_SUPPORT
	bool
	help

config ARCH_HAS_THREAD_LOCAL_STORAGE
	bool
	help

	  storage support.

config ARCH_HAS_DEMAND_PAGING
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has demand paging
	  support.

config ARCH_HAS_RESERVED_PAGE_FRAMES
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has reserved page
	  frames support.

config ARCH_HAS_TIMING_FUNCTIONS
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has timing functions
	  support.

config ARCH_HAS_SYSTICK
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a systick timer.

config ARCH_HAS_CUSTOM_SWAP_TO_MAIN
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a custom swap to

config ARCH_HAS_CUSTOM_BUSY_WAIT
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a custom busy
	  wait function.

config ARCH_HAS_IRQ_VECTOR_TABLE
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has an IRQ vector

config ARCH_HAS_GEN_SW_ISR_TABLE
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a generated

config ARCH_HAS_DYNAMIC_OBJ_LINKING
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has dynamic object

config ARCH_HAS_ADDITIONAL_META_INFO_SECTION
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has an additional

config ARCH_HAS_NO_EXEC_STACK_SUPPORT
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has no-execute stack

config ARCH_HAS_STACK_CANARIES
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has stack canaries

config ARCH_HAS_LAZY_REG_STACK_SWITCH
	bool
	help

config ARCH_HAS_FPU_SHARING
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has FPU sharing

config ARCH_HAS_INTERRUPT_CONTROLLER
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has an interrupt

config ARCH_HAS_THREAD_STACK_SENTINEL
	bool
	help

config ARCH_HAS_EXTRA_EXCEPTION_INFO
	bool
	help

config ARCH_HAS_SW_VECTOR_RELAY
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has software vector

config ARCH_HAS_MULTITHREADING
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has multithreading
	  support.

config ARCH_HAS_PM
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has power management
	  support.

config ARCH_HAS_SINGLE_THREAD_SUPPORT
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has single thread

config ARCH_HAS_ATOMIC_H
	bool
	help

config ARCH_HAS_ATOMIC64_H
	bool
	help

config ARCH_HAS_SET_GDT

config ARCH_HAS_LOG_OUTPUT_SUPPORT

	  This option indicates that the architecture has log output

	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has process execution

config ARCH_HAS_KOBJECT_MEMORY_SLAB
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has kobject memory

	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has kobject alloc

	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has thread statistics

config ARCH_HAS_EXCEPTION_STACK_SIZE
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has an exception

	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has system calls

	  This option indicates that the architecture has instrument

	bool

config ARCH_HAS_THREAD_STRUCT_FIELDS
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has thread struct

config ARCH_HAS_IDLE_HOOK
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has an idle hook.

config ARCH_HAS_ABORT_HANDLER
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has an abort handler.

config ARCH_HAS_SPINLOCK
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has spinlock support.

config ARCH_HAS_UNALIGNED_ACCESS
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has unaligned access
	  support.

config ARCH_HAS_MEM_PROTECT
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has memory protection

config ARCH_HAS_HW_STACK_PROTECTION
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has hardware stack

config ARCH_HAS_ATOMIC_SWAP
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has atomic swap

config ARCH_HAS_ATOMIC_IOP
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has atomic iop

config ARCH_HAS_BUILTIN_STACK_GUARD
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has built-in stack
	  guard support.

config ARCH_HAS_FLUSH_L1_CACHE
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a flush l1 cache
	  function.

config ARCH_HAS_CACHE_FLUSH_ALL
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a cache flush all
	  function.

config ARCH_HAS_CACHE_INVAL_ALL
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a cache invalidate
	  all function.

config ARCH_HAS_CACHE_FLUSH_AND_INVAL_ALL
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a cache flush and
	  invalidate all function.

config ARCH_HAS_CACHE_FLUSH_RANGE
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a cache flush
	  range function.

config ARCH_HAS_CACHE_INVAL_RANGE
	bool
	help
	  This option indicates that the architecture has a cache invalidate

config ARCH_HAS_CACHE_FLUSH_AND_INVAL_RANGE
	bool
	help

menu "Kernel"

config KERNEL_ENTRY
	string "Kernel entry point symbol"
	default "_start"
	help
	  This is the entry point symbol for the kernel.

config INIT_STACKS
	bool "Initialize stack areas"
	default y
	help
	  Enable this option to initialize the stack areas of all threads
	  with a known value (0xaa) before they are started. This is useful
	  for debugging stack overflows.

config THREAD_MONITOR
	bool "Enable thread monitoring"
	help
	  This option enables the thread monitoring feature. When enabled,
	  the kernel will monitor the state of each thread and can report
	  if a thread has been starving for a long time.

config THREAD_NAME
	bool "Enable thread name"
	help
	  Enable this option to be able to name threads. This is useful
	  for debugging.

config THREAD_CUSTOM_DATA
	bool "Enable thread custom data"
	help
	  Enable this option to add a custom data field to the thread
	  control block. This can be used by applications to store
	  per-thread data.

config MAX_THREAD_BYTES
	int "Maximum bytes for thread name"
	depends on THREAD_NAME
	range 3 64
	default 3
	help
	  Maximum number of bytes to reserve for a thread's name.
	  Longer names will be truncated. A null terminator will
	  always be present. Minimum value is 3, to account for
	  at least 2 characters plus a null terminator.

config USERSPACE
	bool "Enable user mode and memory domains"
	select MMU if !CPU_HAS_MMU_FLAG_SUPPORT
	select ARCH_HAS_USERSPACE
	help
	  This option enables user mode and memory domain support. When
	  enabled, threads can be run in user mode with restricted
	  privileges and memory access.

config MEM_POOL_HEAP_BACKEND
	bool "Use memory pool as heap backend"
	depends on HEAP_MEM_POOL_SIZE > 0
	help
	  Enable this option to use a memory pool as the backend for the
	  system heap. This is useful for systems with limited memory.

config HEAP_MEM_POOL_SIZE
	int "Heap memory pool size"
	default 0
	help
	  Size of the heap memory pool in bytes.

config SYS_CLOCK_EXISTS
	bool
	default y
	help
	  This option indicates that a system clock exists.

config SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC

	default 100
	help

	default 40
	help
	  Default priority for kernel initialization objects.

config KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_OBJECTS
	int "Object initialization priority"
	default 30
	help

config KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEVICE

	default 50
	help

	default 20
	help
	  Priority for initializing configuration.

config KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_PRIMARY

	default 10
	help
	  Priority for primary initialization.

config KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_PRE_KERNEL_1
	int "Pre-kernel 1 initialization priority"
	default 0
	help
	  Priority for pre-kernel 1 initialization.

config KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_PRE_KERNEL_2
	int "Pre-kernel 2 initialization priority"
	default 0
	help
	  Priority for pre-kernel 2 initialization.

config KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_POST_KERNEL
	int "Post-kernel initialization priority"
	default 90
	help
	  Priority for post-kernel initialization.

config KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_APPLICATION
	int "Application initialization priority"
	default 99
	help
	  Priority for application initialization.

config MULTITHREADING
	bool "Enable multithreading"
	default y
	select ARCH_HAS_MULTITHREADING
	help
	  Enable this option to support multiple threads.

config NUM_COOP_PRIORITIES
	int "Number of cooperative priorities"
	default 16
	range 0 256
	help
	  Number of cooperative priorities.

config NUM_PREEMPT_PRIORITIES
	int "Number of preemptible priorities"
	default 16
	range 0 256
	help
	  Number of preemptible priorities.

config MAIN_THREAD_PRIORITY
	int "Main thread priority"
	default 0
	help
	  Priority of the main thread.

config IDLE_THREAD_PRIORITY
	int "Idle thread priority"
	default 15
	help
	  Priority of the idle thread.

config MAIN_STACK_SIZE
	int "Main thread stack size"
	default 1024
	help
	  Size of the main thread stack in bytes.

config IDLE_STACK_SIZE
	int "Idle thread stack size"
	default 256
	help
	  Size of the idle thread stack in bytes.

config ISR_STACK_SIZE
	int "ISR stack size"
	default 2048
	help
	  Size of the ISR stack in bytes.

config SYSTEM_WORKQUEUE_STACK_SIZE
	int "System workqueue stack size"
	default 1024
	help
	  Size of the system workqueue stack in bytes.

config SYSTEM_WORKQUEUE_PRIORITY
	int "System workqueue priority"
	default -1
	help
	  Priority of the system workqueue.

config TIMESLICING
	bool "Enable time slicing"
	help
	  Enable this option to allow time slicing of threads with the
	  same priority.

config TIMESLICE_SIZE
	int "Time slice size"
	default 0
	depends on TIMESLICING
	help
	  Time slice size in system clock ticks.

config TIMESLICE_PRIORITY
	int "Time slice priority"
	default 0
	depends on TIMESLICING
	help
	  Highest priority level at which time slicing is performed.

config POLL
	bool "Enable poll API"
	help
	  Enable this option to support the poll() API.

endmenu # Kernel

/*

 *
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

menu "Power management"

config PM
	bool "Power management"
	help
	  Enable power management. This option enables the power management
	  subsystem.

if PM

config PM_DEVICE
	bool "Device Power Management"
	help
	  Enable device power management. This option enables power management
	  for devices. Devices will be suspended when system goes to sleep.
	  They will be resumed when system wakes up.

config PM_DEVICE_RUNTIME
	bool "Device runtime Power Management"
	depends on PM_DEVICE
	help
	  Enable device runtime power management. This option enables power
	  management for devices at runtime.

config PM_CPU_OPS_ON_IDLE
	bool "Enable CPU power management based on idle"
	help
	  Enable power management operations that will be done when the system
	  is idle. This is where the system will enter into one of the
	  supported sleep states.

config PM_SLEEP_STATES
	bool "Enable sleep states"
	depends on PM_CPU_OPS_ON_IDLE
	help
	  Enable power management sleep states. This option allows to put the
	  system into one of the available sleep states when going idle.

if PM_SLEEP_STATES

config PM_DEEP_SLEEP_STATES
	bool "Enable deep sleep states"
	help
	  Enable power management deep sleep states. This option allows to put
	  the system into one of the available deep sleep states when going
	  idle. This is a more involved sleep state where the kernel does not
	  keep track of timing. The system is expected to be woken up by an
	  interrupt.

endif # PM_SLEEP_STATES

config PM_MIN_RESIDENCY_DEFAULT
	int "Default minimum residency for CPU states"
	default 0
	help
	  Default minimum residency in microseconds for CPU power states.
	  A power state is only entered if the time to the next kernel timer
	  event is longer than its minimum residency. This value can be
	  overwritten by the SoC.

config PM_POLICY_CUSTOM
	bool "Custom power management policy"
	help
	  When this option is enabled, the default power management policy is
	  not built. The application is then expected to provide its own
	  power management policy.

if !PM_POLICY_CUSTOM

choice
	prompt "Power management policy"
	default PM_POLICY_RESIDENCY

config PM_POLICY_RESIDENCY
	bool "Residency based power management policy"
	help
	  This policy looks at the residency time of the available power
	  states and chooses the one that best fits the duration of the
	  upcoming idle period.

config PM_POLICY_APP
	bool "Application-specific power management policy"
	help
	  This policy allows the application to be notified of the upcoming
	  idle duration and decide if the system should enter a sleep state.

config PM_POLICY_DUMMY
	bool "Dummy power management policy"
	help
	  This option enables a dummy power management policy. This is useful
	  on platforms that want to enable power management but do not have
	  a policy yet.

endchoice

endif # !PM_POLICY_CUSTOM

endif # PM

endmenu

patch.content:
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

menu "C Library"

source "lib/libc/minimal/Kconfig"
source "lib/libc/picolibc/Kconfig"
source "lib/libc/newlib/Kconfig"

choice
	prompt "C library"
	default MINIMAL_LIBC
	help
	  Select the C library implementation to use.

config MINIMAL_LIBC
	bool "Minimal C library"
	select LIBC_MINIMAL
	help
	  This option enables the minimal C library. This library
	  provides a basic set of C library APIs.

config PICOLIBC
	bool "Picolibc C library"
	select PICOLIBC_SUPPORT
	select SYS_LIBC_HAS_REENT
	help
	  This option enables the Picolibc C library.

config NEWLIB_LIBC
	bool "Newlib C library"
	select NEWLIB_LIBC_SUPPORT
	select SYS_LIBC_HAS_REENT
	help
	  This option enables the Newlib C library.

config EXTERNAL_LIBC
	bool "External C library"
	help
	  This option indicates that an external C library is used.
	  This is automatically selected by toolchains that provide
	  their own C library.

endchoice

config LIBC_MINIMAL
	bool

config PICOLIBC_SUPPORT
	bool

config NEWLIB_LIBC_SUPPORT
	bool

config HAS_LIBC_PLUSPLUS
	bool "C++ library"
	depends on CPLUSPLUS
	help
	  Enable C++ support.

config CPLUSPLUS
	bool

config SYS_LIBC_HAS_REENT
	bool

config MALLOC_ALIGNMENT
	int
	default 8 if 64BIT
	default 4

config STACK_CANARIES
	bool "Compiler stack canaries"
	depends on TOOLCHAIN_HAS_STACK_CANARIES
	help
	  Enable compiler-generated stack canaries to detect stack
	  overflows. When a stack overflow is detected, the kernel
	  will treat it as a fatal error.

config LIBC_ERRNO
	bool "Use libc's errno"
	default y if NEWLIB_LIBC || PICOLIBC
	help
	  Use the C library's errno implementation instead of Zephyr's
	  thread-local implementation. This is required for C libraries
	  that are re-entrant.

config PRINTK
	bool "Enable printk"
	default y
	help
	  This option enables the printk() API, which is a non-standard
	  and simplified version of the standard printf() function.
	  It is used to print formatted strings to the console.

config EARLY_CONSOLE
	bool "Enable early console"
	depends on PRINTK
	help
	  Enable console before kernel is fully initialized.

config STDOUT_CONSOLE
	bool "Redirect stdout to console"
	default y if !(NATIVE_LIBRARY && EXTERNAL_LIBC)
	depends on CONSOLE
	depends on !(NATIVE_LIBRARY && EXTERNAL_LIBC)
	help
	  Redirect stdout to the console device. This makes functions
	  like printf() output to the system console.

endmenu

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

menu "C Library"

source "lib/libc/minimal/Kconfig"
source "lib/libc/picolibc/Kconfig"
source "lib/libc/newlib/Kconfig"

choice
	prompt "C library"
	default MINIMAL_LIBC
	help
	  Select the C library implementation to use.

config MINIMAL_LIBC
	bool "Minimal C library"
	select LIBC_MINIMAL
	help
	  This option enables the minimal C library. This library
	  provides a basic set of C library APIs.

config PICOLIBC
	bool "Picolibc C library"
	select PICOLIBC_SUPPORT
	select SYS_LIBC_HAS_REENT
	help
	  This option enables the Picolibc C library.

config NEWLIB_LIBC
	bool "Newlib C library"
	select NEWLIB_LIBC_SUPPORT
	select SYS_LIBC_HAS_REENT
	help
	  This option enables the Newlib C library.

config EXTERNAL_LIBC
	bool "External C library"
	help
	  This option indicates that an external C library is used.
	  This is automatically selected by toolchains that provide
	  their own C library.

endchoice

config LIBC_MINIMAL
	bool

config PICOLIBC_SUPPORT
	bool

config NEWLIB_LIBC_SUPPORT
	bool

config HAS_LIBC_PLUSPLUS
	bool "C++ library"
	depends on CPLUSPLUS
	help
	  Enable C++ support.

config CPLUSPLUS
	bool

config SYS_LIBC_HAS_REENT
	bool

config MALLOC_ALIGNMENT
	int
	default 8 if 64BIT
	default 4

config STACK_CANARIES
	bool "Compiler stack canaries"
	depends on TOOLCHAIN_HAS_STACK_CANARIES
	help
	  Enable compiler-generated stack canaries to detect stack
	  overflows. When a stack overflow is detected, the kernel
	  will treat it as a fatal error.

config LIBC_ERRNO
	bool "Use libc's errno"
	default y if NEWLIB_LIBC || PICOLIBC
	help
	  Use the C library's errno implementation instead of Zephyr's
	  thread-local implementation. This is required for C libraries
	  that are re-entrant.

config PRINTK
	bool "Enable printk"
	default y
	help
	  This option enables the printk() API, which is a non-standard
	  and simplified version of the standard printf() function.
	  It is used to print formatted strings to the console.

config EARLY_CONSOLE
	bool "Enable early console"
	depends on PRINTK
	help
	  Enable console before kernel is fully initialized.

config STDOUT_CONSOLE
	bool "Redirect stdout to console"
	default y if !(NATIVE_LIBRARY && EXTERNAL_LIBC)
	depends on CONSOLE
	depends on !(NATIVE_LIBRARY && EXTERNAL_LIBC)
	help
	  Redirect stdout to the console device. This makes functions
	  like printf() output to the system console.

endmenu

# Power management configuration options

# Copyright (c) 2018-2023, Intel Corporation.
# Copyright (c) 2023, Nordic Semiconductor ASA
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

menu "Power management"

config PM
	bool "Enable power management"
	help
	  Enable power management. This option enables the power management
	  subsystem.

if PM

config PM_DEVICE
	bool "Enable device power management"
	default y
	help
	  Enable device power management. This option enables the device
	  power management infrastructure. The SoC power management will be
	  kept active and it will be possible to suspend/resume devices.

config PM_DEVICE_RUNTIME
	bool "Enable device runtime power management"
	depends on PM_DEVICE
	help
	  Enable device runtime power management. This option enables the
	  device runtime power management infrastructure that allows devices
	  to be automatically suspended when not in use and resumed when
	  needed.

config PM_CPU_OPS_PSCI
	bool "Enable PSCI CPU power operations"
	depends on ARM64 && GIC_V2
	select ARM_PSCI
	help
	  Enable CPU power management operations using PSCI.

config PM_S2RAM
	bool "Enable System Suspend to RAM"
	depends on PM_DEVICE
	help
	  Enable system suspend to RAM support. This requires a platform that
	  is capable of saving and restoring its state.

config PM_POLICY_RESIDENCY
	bool "Residency policy"
	help
	  With this policy the system will try to enter the deepest possible
	  power state based on the ticks spent in idle.

config PM_POLICY_APP
	bool "Application-specific policy"
	help
	  With this policy the application can have some control over power
	  management. The application can decide which power states can be
	  used.

choice
	prompt "Power management policy"
	default PM_POLICY_RESIDENCY

config PM_POLICY_DUMMY
	bool "Dummy policy"
	help
	  This policy can be used by applications which do not require any
	  specific power management policy but want to be able to get/release
	  the CPU power constraints.

source "subsys/pm/policy/Kconfig"

endchoice

config PM_MIN_RESIDENCY_US
	int "Minimum residency for a power state to be used"
	default 0
	help
	  Some SoCs take a certain amount of time to enter and exit a
	  power state. If the time spent in idle is less than this, it is
	  not worth entering the state. This is SoC specific. The value
	  is in microseconds.

config PM_TICKLESS_IDLE
	bool "Enable tickless idle"
	depends on TICKLESS_IDLE
	default y
	help
	  Enable tickless idle in power management. This option is only
	  effective if the kernel supports tickless idle.

config PM_TICKLESS_IDLE_FALLBACK
	bool "Fallback to tickful idle if tickless is not effective"
	depends on PM_TICKLESS_IDLE
	help
	  Fallback to tickful idle if the duration of the idle period is
	  too short for tickless idle to be effective. This is useful
	  for systems that have a high overhead for entering and exiting
	  tickless idle.

config PM_LOG_LEVEL_OFF
	bool "No logging"
	depends on LOG
	help
	  Do not write any log messages.

config PM_LOG_LEVEL_ERR
	bool "Error"
	depends on LOG
	help
	  Write only error messages.

config PM_LOG_LEVEL_WRN
	bool "Warning"
	depends on LOG
	help
	  Write error and warning messages.

config PM_LOG_LEVEL_INF
	bool "Info"
	depends on LOG
	help
	  Write error, warning and info messages.

config PM_LOG_LEVEL_DBG
	bool "Debug"
	depends on LOG
	help
	  Write error, warning, info and debug messages.

config PM_LOG_LEVEL
	int
	default 0 if PM_LOG_LEVEL_OFF
	default 1 if PM_LOG_LEVEL_ERR
	default 2 if PM_LOG_LEVEL_WRN
	default 3 if PM_LOG_LEVEL_INF
	default 4 if PM_LOG_LEVEL_DBG
	depends on LOG

config PM_LOG
	bool
	default y if PM_LOG_LEVEL > 0
	depends on LOG

endif # PM

endmenu

#ifndef ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_
#define ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_

#include <zephyr/kernel.h>
#include <zephyr/ztest.h>
#include <zephyr/sys/iterable_sections.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/**
 * @brief Ztest testing framework
 * @defgroup ztest_test Ztest testing framework
 * @ingroup ztest
 * @{
 */

extern const struct ztest_arch_api ztest_api;

struct ztest_unit_test {
	const char *name;
	ztest_test_t test;
	ztest_setup_t setup;
	ztest_teardown_t teardown;
#ifdef CONFIG_ZTEST_TEST_STATS
	struct ztest_unit_test_stats *stats;
#endif
};

#ifdef CONFIG_ZTEST_TEST_STATS
struct ztest_unit_test_stats {
	struct ztest_unit_test *test;
	uint32_t run_count;
	uint32_t skip_count;
	uint32_t fail_count;
	uint64_t duration_ns;
};
#endif

#if defined(CONFIG_ZTEST_SHUFFLE)
#define ZTEST_DMEM
#else
#define ZTEST_DMEM __ztest_test_data
#endif

#ifndef __ztest_test_suite_name
#define __ztest_test_suite_name
#endif

#ifdef CONFIG_ZTEST_TEST_STATS
/* Forward declaration */
struct ztest_unit_test_stats;

#define Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_STATS_NAME(suite, test) z_ztest_unit_test_stats__##suite##__##test
#define Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_NAME(suite, test) z_ztest_unit_test__##suite##__##test
#else
#define Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_STATS_NAME(suite, test) z_ztest_unit_test__##suite##__##test
#define Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_NAME(suite, test) z_ztest_unit_test__##suite##__##test
#endif

#define z_ztest_unit_test_setup_teardown(fn, setup, teardown)                                      \
	static ZTEST_DMEM struct ztest_unit_test Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_NAME(                               \
		__ztest_test_suite_name, fn) = {                                                      \
		.name = #fn, .test = fn, .setup = setup, .teardown = teardown,                       \
		IF_ENABLED(CONFIG_ZTEST_TEST_STATS, (.stats = NULL,))                                \
	};                                                                                       \
	STRUCT_SECTION_ITERABLE(ztest_unit_test, Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_NAME(                         \
							__ztest_test_suite_name, fn))

#ifdef CONFIG_ZTEST_TEST_STATS
#define ztest_unit_test_with_stats(fn)                                                             \
	static ZTEST_DMEM struct ztest_unit_test Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_NAME(                              \
		__ztest_test_suite_name, fn) = {.name = #fn, .test = fn, .stats = NULL};            \
	static ZTEST_DMEM struct ztest_unit_test_stats Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_STATS_NAME(                  \
		__ztest_test_suite_name, fn) = {                                                   \
		.test = &Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_NAME(__ztest_test_suite_name, fn),                       \
	};                                                                                         \
	static void z_ztest_register_test_stats_##__ztest_test_suite_name##__##fn(void)             \
	{                                                                                          \
		Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_NAME(__ztest_test_suite_name, fn).stats =                        \
			&Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_STATS_NAME(__ztest_test_suite_name, fn);                \
	}                                                                                          \
	Z_TEST_REGISTER_TEST_STATS(z_ztest_register_test_stats_##__ztest_test_suite_name##__##fn)

#define ztest_unit_test_setup_teardown_with_stats(fn, setup, teardown)                             \
	static ZTEST_DMEM struct ztest_unit_test Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_NAME(                              \
		__ztest_test_suite_name, fn) = {                                                   \
		.name = #fn, .test = fn, .setup = setup, .teardown = teardown, .stats = NULL};     \
	static ZTEST_DMEM struct ztest_unit_test_stats Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_STATS_NAME(                  \
		__ztest_test_suite_name, fn) = {                                                   \
		.test = &Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_NAME(__ztest_test_suite_name, fn),                       \
	};                                                                                         \
	static void z_ztest_register_test_stats_##__ztest_test_suite_name##__##fn(void)             \
	{                                                                                          \
		Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_NAME(__ztest_test_suite_name, fn).stats =                        \
			&Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_STATS_NAME(__ztest_test_suite_name, fn);                \
	}                                                                                          \
	Z_TEST_REGISTER_TEST_STATS(z_ztest_register_test_stats_##__ztest_test_suite_name##__##fn)
#endif

/**
 * @brief Define a test case.
 *
 * @details This macro defines a test case, which can be later added to a test
 * suite. This should not be used directly. Use @ref ztest_unit_test or
 * @ref ztest_unit_test_setup_teardown instead.
 */
#ifdef CONFIG_ZTEST_TEST_STATS
#define ztest_unit_test(fn) ztest_unit_test_with_stats(fn)
#else
#define ztest_unit_test(fn)                                                                        \
	z_ztest_unit_test_setup_teardown(fn, ztest_empty_setup, ztest_empty_teardown)
#endif

/**
 * @brief Define a test case with setup and teardown functions.
 *
 * @details This macro defines a test case with setup and teardown functions,
 * which can be later added to a test suite. The setup function will be called
 * before the test case is executed, and the teardown function will be called
 * after the test case is executed. This should not be used directly. Use
 * @ref ztest_unit_test or @ref ztest_unit_test_setup_teardown instead.
 */
#ifdef CONFIG_ZTEST_TEST_STATS
#define ztest_unit_test_setup_teardown(fn, setup, teardown)                                        \
	ztest_unit_test_setup_teardown_with_stats(fn, setup, teardown)
#else
#define ztest_unit_test_setup_teardown(fn, setup, teardown)                                        \
	z_ztest_unit_test_setup_teardown(fn, setup, teardown)
#endif

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite.
 *
 * @details This macro defines a test suite, which is a collection of test
 * cases. The test suite will be executed by the test runner. Test cases must
 * be defined within the call to this macro.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param ... A list of test cases, separated by commas.
 */
#define ztest_test_suite(suite, ...)                                                               \
	static const char *Z_TEST_SUITE_NAME = #suite;                                           \
	static const char __ztest_test_suite_name[] = #suite;                                    \
	void z_ztest_run_test_suite_##suite(const void *p)                                       \
	{                                                                                        \
		ztest_run_tests((const struct ztest_unit_test *)__ztest_unit_test_start,              \
				(const struct ztest_unit_test *)__ztest_unit_test_end, #suite);           \
	}

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite with a predicate.
 *
 * @details This macro defines a test suite that will only be executed if the
 * predicate is true. This is useful for tests that depend on a certain
 * configuration or hardware. The test suite will be executed by the test
 * runner. Test cases must be defined within the call to this macro.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param predicate A boolean expression that determines if the test suite
 * should be executed.
 * @param ... A list of test cases, separated by commas.
 */
#define ztest_test_suite_predicate(suite, predicate, ...)                                          \
	static const char *Z_TEST_SUITE_NAME = #suite;                                           \
	static const char __ztest_test_suite_name[] = #suite;                                    \
	void z_ztest_run_test_suite_##suite(const void *p)                                       \
	{                                                                                        \
		if (predicate) {                                                                       \
			ztest_run_tests((const struct ztest_unit_test *)__ztest_unit_test_start,          \
					(const struct ztest_unit_test *)__ztest_unit_test_end, #suite);       \
		} else {                                                                               \
			ztest_test_skip();                                                                 \
		}                                                                                      \
	}

/**
 * @brief Run a test suite.
 *
 * @details This macro runs a test suite. This is usually called from the main
 * function of the test application.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 */
#define ztest_run_test_suite(suite)                                                                \
	z_ztest_run_test_suite_##suite(NULL)

/**
 * @} ztest_test
 */

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_ */

#ifndef ZEPHYR_INCLUDE_TOOLCHAIN_GCC_H_
#define ZEPHYR_INCLUDE_TOOLCHAIN_GCC_H_


#include <zephyr/toolchain/common.h>

#if !defined(__ASSEMBLER__)

#include <stddef.h>

/*
 * The gcc-version.h header is not available before gcc 5.0.0.
 * The __GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__ is not available before gcc 3.0.0.
 */
#if __GNUC__ >= 5
#include <gcc-version.h>
#endif

#ifndef __GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__
#define __GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__ 0
#endif

#define GCC_VERSION (__GNUC__ * 10000 \
		   + __GNUC_MINOR__ * 100 \
		   + __GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__)

#if (GCC_VERSION < 40800)
#error "Zephyr requires GCC 4.8.0 or higher"
#endif

#undef __in_section
#define __in_section(sect) __attribute__((section("." #sect)))

#undef __in_section_unique
#define __in_section_unique(sect) __attribute__((section("." #sect "." __FILE__ "." __func__ "." STRINGIFY(__LINE__))))

#define __in_section_named(sect) __attribute__((section(sect)))

#define __no_optimization __attribute__((optimize("-O0")))
#define __no_inline __attribute__((noinline))
#define __used __attribute__((__used__))
#define __unused __attribute__((__unused__))
#define __maybe_unused __attribute__((__unused__))
#define __deprecated __attribute__((deprecated))
#define __fallthrough __attribute__((fallthrough))

#define Z_INTERNAL_DEPRECATED_MACRO_CAT(a, b) a##b
#define Z_INTERNAL_DEPRECATED_MACRO_CAT2(a, b) Z_INTERNAL_DEPRECATED_MACRO_CAT(a, b)
#define Z_INTERNAL_DEPRECATED_MACRO_UNIQUE_NAME(prefix) \
	Z_INTERNAL_DEPRECATED_MACRO_CAT2(prefix, __COUNTER__)

#if defined(CONFIG_WARN_DEPRECATED) && !defined(__DEPRECATE_MACROS)

#define __DEPRECATED_MACRO(macro, msg) \
	__DEPRECATED_MACRO_NAMED(STRINGIFY(macro), macro, msg)

/* The use of a statement expression is deliberate.
 *
 * 1. It allows the macro to be used in any context where an expression is
 *    valid, and not just as a standalone statement.
 * 2. It creates a new scope for the static inline function.
 *
 * The use of a static inline function is also deliberate.
 *
 * 1. It allows the compiler to issue a warning when the macro is used.
 * 2. It is defined as static inline so that the compiler can optimize it away.
 *
 * The use of __COUNTER__ is to ensure that the function name is unique, which
 * is necessary to avoid name clashes when the macro is used multiple times
 * in the same scope.
 *
 * The use of if (false) is to suppress the unused warning for the macro
 * parameter. When `macro` is a function-like macro, (void)macro results in a
 * call to the macro with no arguments, which is often a compilation error.
 * The if (false) block is never executed, but the compiler still parses it
 * and sees that the macro is "used".
 */
#define __DEPRECATED_MACRO_NAMED(name, macro, msg) \
	({ \
		__attribute__((deprecated(msg " (" #name ")"))) \
		static inline void Z_INTERNAL_DEPRECATED_MACRO_UNIQUE_NAME(_deprecated_macro_)(void) {}; \
		if (false) { \
			(void)Z_INTERNAL_DEPRECATED_MACRO_UNIQUE_NAME(_deprecated_macro_); \
			(void)macro; \
		} \
		macro; \
	})

#else /* !CONFIG_WARN_DEPRECATED || __DEPRECATE_MACROS */

#define __DEPRECATED_MACRO(macro, msg) macro
#define __DEPRECATED_MACRO_NAMED(name, macro, msg) macro

#endif /* CONFIG_WARN_DEPRECATED && !__DEPRECATE_MACROS */

#define __weak __attribute__((__weak__))
#define __packed __attribute__((__packed__))
#define __aligned(x) __attribute__((__aligned__(x)))
#define __printf_like(f, a)   __attribute__((format(printf, f, a)))
#define __scanf_like(f, a)   __attribute__((format(scanf, f, a)))

#define ARG_UNUSED(x) (void)(x)

/*
 * These macros are used to suppress "-Wunused-parameter" warnings, but only
 * if the toolchain supports the __unused attribute.
 */
#define UNUSED_PARAM(x) x __maybe_unused
#define UNUSED_PARAMS(...) FOR_EACH(UNUSED_PARAM, (,), __VA_ARGS__)

#define __no_return __attribute__((__noreturn__))

#define __ramfunc __in_section(ramfunc)

#define __rom __in_section(romfunc)

#define __noret __no_return

#define __weak_func __weak

#define __kernel __in_section(kernel)

#define __user

#define __force_inline inline __attribute__((always_inline))

#define __nocast

#define __subsystem

#if defined(CONFIG_STACK_CANARIES)
#define __stack_no_check __attribute__((no_stack_protector))
#else
#define __stack_no_check
#endif

#define popcount(x) __builtin_popcount(x)

#include <zephyr/toolchain/gcc_builtin.h>

#endif /* !__ASSEMBLER__ */

#endif /* ZEPHYR_INCLUDE_TOOLCHAIN_GCC_H_ */

/**
 * @file
 *
 * @brief Zephyr testing assertion macros.
 */

#ifndef ZEPHYR_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_ASSERT_H_
#define ZEPHYR_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_ASSERT_H_

#include <zephyr/ztest.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/**
 * @brief Assert that a condition is true.
 *
 * The zassert_true() macro asserts that the @a cond expression is true.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param cond Condition to check.
 * @param msg Optional message to print if the assertion fails.
 */
#define zassert_true(cond, msg, ...) \
	zassert(cond, msg, ##__VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Assert that a condition is false.
 *
 * The zassert_false() macro asserts that the @a cond expression is false.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param cond Condition to check.
 * @param msg Optional message to print if the assertion fails.
 */
#define zassert_false(cond, msg, ...) \
	zassert(!(cond), msg, ##__VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Assert that a condition is null.
 *
 * The zassert_is_null() macro asserts that the @a cond expression is null.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param cond Condition to check.
 * @param msg Optional message to print if the assertion fails.
 */
#define zassert_is_null(cond, msg, ...) \
	zassert((cond) == NULL, msg, ##__VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Assert that a condition is not null.
 *
 * The zassert_not_null() macro asserts that the @a cond expression is not null.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param cond Condition to check.
 * @param msg Optional message to print if the assertion fails.
 */
#define zassert_not_null(cond, msg, ...) \
	zassert((cond) != NULL, msg, ##__VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Assert that two integers are equal.
 *
 * The zassert_equal() macro asserts that the two integers @a a and @a b are
 * equal.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param a First integer.
 * @param b Second integer.
 * @param msg Optional message to print if the assertion fails.
 */
#define zassert_equal(a, b, msg, ...) \
	zassert((a) == (b), msg, ##__VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Assert that two integers are not equal.
 *
 * The zassert_not_equal() macro asserts that the two integers @a a and @a b are
 * not equal.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param a First integer.
 * @param b Second integer.
 * @param msg Optional message to print if the assertion fails.
 */
#define zassert_not_equal(a, b, msg, ...) \
	zassert((a) != (b), msg, ##__VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Assert that two memory buffers have the same contents.
 *
 * The zassert_mem_equal() macro asserts that the @a len bytes of the two memory
 * buffers @a buf1 and @a buf2 have the same contents.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param buf1 First memory buffer.
 * @param buf2 Second memory buffer.
 * @param len Number of bytes to compare.
 * @param msg Optional message to print if the assertion fails.
 */
#define zassert_mem_equal(buf1, buf2, len, msg, ...) \
	zassert_true(memcmp(buf1, buf2, len) == 0, msg, ##__VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Assert that two memory buffers have different contents.
 *
 * The zassert_mem_not_equal() macro asserts that the @a len bytes of the two
 * memory buffers @a buf1 and @a buf2 have different contents.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param buf1 First memory buffer.
 * @param buf2 Second memory buffer.
 * @param len Number of bytes to compare.
 * @param msg Optional message to print if the assertion fails.
 */
#define zassert_mem_not_equal(buf1, buf2, len, msg, ...) \
	zassert_true(memcmp(buf1, buf2, len) != 0, msg, ##__VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Assert that two memory buffers have the same contents, with string-like details.
 *
 * This is equivalent to zassert_mem_equal(), but if the assertion fails, the
 * details will be printed as if the buffers were strings. This is useful for
 * comparing buffers that are not NUL-terminated.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param buf1 First memory buffer.
 * @param buf2 Second memory buffer.
 * @param len Number of bytes to compare.
 * @param msg Optional message to print if the assertion fails.
 */
#define zassert_mem_equal_str(buf1, buf2, len, msg, ...) \
	do { \
		const char *b1 = (const char *)buf1; \
		const char *b2 = (const char *)buf2; \
		if (memcmp(b1, b2, len) != 0) { \
			ztest_print_str_equal(b1, b2, len); \
			ztest_fail_message(msg, ##__VA_ARGS__); \
		} \
	} while (0)

/**
 * @brief Assert that two strings are equal.
 *
 * The zassert_str_equal() macro asserts that the two strings @a s1 and @a s2
 * are equal.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param s1 First string.
 * @param s2 Second string.
 * @param msg Optional message to print if the assertion fails.
 */
#define zassert_str_equal(s1, s2, msg, ...) \
	do { \
		const char *s1_ = (s1); \
		const char *s2_ = (s2); \
		if (strcmp(s1_, s2_) != 0) { \
			ztest_print_str_equal(s1_, s2_, 0); \
			ztest_fail_message(msg, ##__VA_ARGS__); \
		} \
	} while (0)

/**
 * @brief Assert that two strings are not equal.
 *
 * The zassert_str_not_equal() macro asserts that the two strings @a s1 and @a s2
 * are not equal.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param s1 First string.
 * @param s2 Second string.
 * @param msg Optional message to print if the assertion fails.
 */
#define zassert_str_not_equal(s1, s2, msg, ...) \
	zassert_true(strcmp(s1, s2) != 0, msg, ##__VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Assert that a pointer is within a given memory buffer.
 *
 * The zassert_within() macro asserts that the pointer @a ptr is within the
 * buffer starting at @a base of size @a size.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param ptr Pointer.
 * @param base Start of the buffer.
 * @param size Size of the buffer.
 * @param msg Optional message to print if the assertion fails.
 */
#define zassert_within(ptr, base, size, msg, ...) \
	zassert((ptr) >= (base) && (ptr) < ((base) + (size)), msg, ##__VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Assert that a pointer is not within a given memory buffer.
 *
 * The zassert_not_within() macro asserts that the pointer @a ptr is not within
 * the buffer starting at @a base of size @a size.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param ptr Pointer.
 * @param base Start of the buffer.
 * @param size Size of the buffer.
 * @param msg Optional message to print if the assertion fails.
 */
#define zassert_not_within(ptr, base, size, msg, ...) \
	zassert(!((ptr) >= (base) && (ptr) < ((base) + (size))), msg, ##__VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Unconditionally fail a test.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param msg Optional message to print.
 */
#define zassert_unreachable(msg, ...) \
	zassert(0, msg, ##__VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Assert that two float numbers are equal.
 *
 * The zassert_float_equal() macro asserts that the two float numbers @a a and @a b are
 * equal.
 *
 * If the assertion fails, the test function is terminated.
 *
 * @param a First float number.
 * @param b Second float number.

/*

 */

#ifndef ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_
#define ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_

#include <zephyr/ztest.h>
#include <zephyr/sys/iterable_sections.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/**
 * @defgroup ztest_test_deprecated Ztest testing macros (deprecated)
 * @ingroup ztest
 *
 * @brief Ztest testing macros.
 *
 * @deprecated In favor of the new API, see @ref ztest_new_api.
 *
 * @{
 */

/**
 * @brief Define a test case.
 *
 * @param name The test case's name.
 * @param fn The test case's function.
 */
#define ztest_test_case(name, fn) \
	static void fn(void); \
	REGISTER_TEST_CASE(name, fn, 0)

/**
 * @brief Define a user test case.
 *
 * @param name The test case's name.
 * @param fn The test case's function.
 */
#define ztest_user_test_case(name, fn) \
	static void fn(void); \
	REGISTER_TEST_CASE(name, fn, 1)

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite.
 *
 * @param suite The test suite's name.
 * @param ... A list of `ztest_unit_test` to be included in the suite.
 */
#define ztest_test_suite(suite, ...) \
	static struct ztest_unit_test suite[] = { \
		__VA_ARGS__, \
		ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_END \
	}; \
	STRUCT_SECTION_ITERABLE(ztest_suite_node, _ztest_suite_##suite) = { \
		.name = #suite, \
		.unit_tests = suite \
	}

/**
 * @}
 */

/**
 * @defgroup ztest_new_api Ztest new testing API
 * @ingroup ztest
 *
 * @brief Ztest testing macros.
 *
 * This API is a replacement for the now deprecated @ref ztest_test_deprecated.
 *
 * @{
 */

/**
 * @brief Define a test function with setup and teardown.
 *
 * @param fn The test function's name.
 * @param setup The setup function's name.
 * @param teardown The teardown function's name.
 */
#define Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(fn, setup, teardown) \
	{ \
		.name = #fn, \
		.test = fn, \
		.setup = setup, \
		.teardown = teardown, \
	}

/**
 * @brief Define a test function.
 *
 * @param fn The test function's name.
 */
#define ztest_unit_test(fn) \
	Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(fn, NULL, NULL)

/**
 * @brief Define a test function with a setup function.
 *
 * @param fn The test function's name.
 * @param setup The setup function's name.
 */
#define ztest_unit_test_setup(fn, setup) \
	Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(fn, setup, NULL)

/**
 * @brief Define a test function with a teardown function.
 *
 * @param fn The test function's name.
 * @param teardown The teardown function's name.
 */
#define ztest_unit_test_teardown(fn, teardown) \
	Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(fn, NULL, teardown)

/**
 * @brief Define a test function with setup and teardown functions.
 *
 * @param fn The test function's name.
 * @param setup The setup function's name.
 * @param teardown The teardown function's name.
 */
#define ztest_unit_test_setup_teardown(fn, setup, teardown) \
	Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(fn, setup, teardown)

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite with setup and teardown.
 *
 * @internal
 *
 * @param suite The test suite's name.
 * @param setup The setup function's name.
 * @param teardown The teardown function's name.
 * @param ... A list of `ztest_unit_test` to be included in the suite.
 */
#define Z_ZTEST_TEST_SUITE_DEFINE(suite, setup, teardown, ...) \
	static struct ztest_unit_test _ztest_unit_test_##suite[] = { \
		__VA_ARGS__ \
	}; \
	STRUCT_SECTION_ITERABLE(ztest_suite_node, _ztest_suite_##suite) = { \
		.name = #suite, \
		.unit_tests = _ztest_unit_test_##suite, \
		.count = ARRAY_SIZE(_ztest_unit_test_##suite), \
		.setup = setup, \
		.teardown = teardown, \
	}

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite.
 *
 * @param suite The test suite's name.
 * @param ... A list of `ztest_unit_test` to be included in the suite.
 */
#define ztest_new_test_suite(suite, ...) \
	Z_ZTEST_TEST_SUITE_DEFINE(suite, NULL, NULL, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite with setup and teardown functions.
 *
 * @param suite The test suite's name.
 * @param setup The setup function's name.
 * @param teardown The teardown function's name.
 * @param ... A list of `ztest_unit_test` to be included in the suite.
 */
#define ztest_test_suite_with_setup_teardown(suite, setup, teardown, ...) \
	Z_ZTEST_TEST_SUITE_DEFINE(suite, setup, teardown, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Define a simple asynchronous test function.
 *
 * This macro is used to define a simple asynchronous test function that uses a single
 * k_sem to signal completion.
 *
 * @param fn The test function's name.
 */
#define ztest_simple_async_test(fn) \
	static K_SEM_DEFINE(async_sem, 0, 1); \
	static void fn(void *data)

/**
 * @brief End a simple asynchronous test function.
 *
 * This macro is used to end a simple asynchronous test function and wait for the
 * completion signal.
 */
#define ztest_async_test_end() \
	k_sem_take(&async_sem, K_FOREVER)

/**
 * @brief Signal completion of a simple asynchronous test function.
 *
 * This macro is used to signal the completion of a simple asynchronous test function.
 */
#define ztest_async_test_signal() \
	k_sem_give(&async_sem)

/**
 * @}
 */

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_ */

#ifndef ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_
#define ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_

#include <zephyr/kernel.h>
#include <zephyr/ztest.h>
#include <zephyr/sys/iterable_sections.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* For test registration */
#ifdef CONFIG_ZTEST_MULTITHREADING
#define ZTEST_DMEM K_APP_DMEM(ztest_mem_partition)
#define ZTEST_BMEM K_APP_BMEM(ztest_mem_partition)
extern K_MEM_PARTITION_DEFINE(ztest_mem_partition, NULL, 0, 0);
#else
#define ZTEST_DMEM
#define ZTEST_BMEM
#endif

struct ztest_stats {
	int pass;
	int fail;
	int skip;
};

struct ztest_unit_test {
	const char *name;
	void (*test)(void *data);
	void (*setup)(void *data);
	void (*teardown)(void *data);
	void *user_data;
	void *fixture;
	struct ztest_stats *stats;
};

/* Forward declaration */
struct ztest_suite_stats;

struct ztest_test_suite {
	const char *name;
	bool (*predicate)(const void *data);
	void (*setup)(void *data);
	void (*teardown)(void *data);
	void (*before)(void *data);
	void (*after)(void *data);
	void *user_data;
	void *fixture;
	struct ztest_suite_stats *stats;
};

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite.
 *
 * This macro defines a test suite with a given name and registers it for the
 * test framework.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param predicate A function that returns true if the suite should be run.
 * @param setup A function to run before the suite.
 * @param before A function to run before each test in the suite.
 * @param after A function to run after each test in the suite.
 * @param teardown A function to run after the suite.
 */
#define ZTEST_SUITE(suite, predicate, setup, before, after, teardown)                   \
	static ZTEST_DMEM struct ztest_suite_stats z_ztest_suite_stats__##suite;             \
	static ZTEST_DMEM struct ztest_test_suite z_ztest_test_suite__##suite = {            \
		.name = #suite,                                                                 \
		.predicate = predicate,                                                         \
		.setup = setup,                                                                 \
		.teardown = teardown,                                                           \
		.before = before,                                                               \
		.after = after,                                                                 \
		.stats = &z_ztest_suite_stats__##suite,                                         \
	};                                                                                  \
	Z_STRUCT_SECTION_ITERABLE(ztest_test_suite, z_ztest_test_suite__##suite)

#define _ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_INITIALIZER(suite, test, setup_fn, teardown_fn, user, fixture)     \
	static void test_##suite##_##test(void *data);                                     \
	static ZTEST_DMEM struct ztest_stats z_ztest_unit_test_stats__##suite##__##test;     \
	static ZTEST_DMEM struct ztest_unit_test z_ztest_unit_test__##suite##__##test = {    \
		.name = #test,                                                                  \
		.test = test_##suite##_##test,                                                  \
		.setup = setup_fn,                                                              \
		.teardown = teardown_fn,                                                        \
		.stats = &z_ztest_unit_test_stats__##suite##__##test,                            \
		.user_data = user,                                                              \
		.fixture = fixture,                                                             \
	};                                                                                  \
	Z_STRUCT_SECTION_ITERABLE(ztest_unit_test, z_ztest_unit_test__##suite##__##test)

#define _ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(suite, test, setup, teardown, user, fixture)        \
	_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_INITIALIZER(suite, test, setup, teardown, user, fixture);          \
	static void test_##suite##_##test(void *data)

/**
 * @brief Define a test case.
 *
 * This is the vanilla version of the test case macro.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param test The name of the test.
 */
#define ztest_unit_test(suite, test) \
	_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(suite, test, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL)

/**
 * @brief Define a test case that uses user data.
 *
 * This version of the test case macro allows the user to pass a void pointer
 * to their test function.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param test The name of the test.
 * @param user_data A void pointer to be passed to the test function.
 */
#define ztest_user_unit_test(suite, test, user_data) \
	_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(suite, test, NULL, NULL, user_data, NULL)

/**
 * @brief Define a test case with setup and teardown functions.
 *
 * This version of the test case macro allows the user to specify setup and
 * teardown functions to be run before and after the test.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param test The name of the test.
 * @param setup The setup function.
 * @param teardown The teardown function.
 */
#define ztest_unit_test_setup_teardown(suite, test, setup, teardown) \
	_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(suite, test, setup, teardown, NULL, NULL)

/**
 * @brief Define a test case with setup and teardown functions that uses user data.
 *
 * This version of the test case macro allows the user to specify setup and
 * teardown functions to be run before and after the test, and to pass a void
 * pointer to their test function.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param test The name of the test.
 * @param setup The setup function.
 * @param teardown The teardown function.
 * @param user_data A void pointer to be passed to the test function.
 */
#define ztest_user_unit_test_setup_teardown(suite, test, setup, teardown, user_data) \
	_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(suite, test, setup, teardown, user_data, NULL)

/**
 * @brief Define a test that has a parameter.
 *
 * This is useful for tests that are very similar and only vary by a parameter.
 * The parameter is passed to the test function as a void pointer.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param test The name of the test.
 * @param data The parameter to pass to the test function.
 */
#define ztest_unit_test_with_data(suite, test, data) \
	_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(suite, test, NULL, NULL, (void *)data, NULL)

/**
 * @brief Define a test fixture.
 *
 * This macro defines a test fixture with a given name.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param ... The fixture data.
 */
#define ztest_register_fixture(suite, ...) \
	static ZTEST_DMEM struct suite##_fixture z_ztest_fixture__##suite = {__VA_ARGS__}

/**
 * @brief Define a test that uses a fixture.
 *
 * This macro defines a test that uses a fixture.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param test The name of the test.
 */
#define ztest_fixture_unit_test(suite, test) \
	_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(suite, test, ztest_fixture_setup, \
					ztest_fixture_teardown, NULL, &z_ztest_fixture__##suite)

/**
 * @brief Define a test that uses a fixture and has setup and teardown functions.
 *
 * This macro defines a test that uses a fixture and has setup and teardown
 * functions.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param test The name of the test.
 * @param setup The setup function.
 * @param teardown The teardown function.
 */
#define ztest_fixture_unit_test_setup_teardown(suite, test, setup, teardown) \
	_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(suite, test, setup, teardown, NULL, \
					&z_ztest_fixture__##suite)

/**
 * @brief Get the fixture for the current test.
 *
 * @param type The type of the fixture.
 * @return A pointer to the fixture.
 */
#define ztest_get_fixture(type) ((type *)ztest_get_user_data())

/**
 * @brief The setup function for a test that uses a fixture.
 *
 * @param data A pointer to the user data.
 */
static inline void ztest_fixture_setup(void *data)
{
	ztest_set_user_data(data);
}

/**
 * @brief The teardown function for a test that uses a fixture.
 *
 * @param data A pointer to the user data.
 */
static inline void ztest_fixture_teardown(void *data)
{
	ARG_UNUSED(data);
	ztest_set_user_data(NULL);
}

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_ */

# Ztest is not needed, but it is used to show test statistics
CONFIG_ZTEST=y
CONFIG_ZTEST_NEW_API=y

# Enable the mcumgr transport protocol
CONFIG_MCUMGR=y

# Enable the Shell mcumgr transport.
CONFIG_MCUMGR_TRANSPORT_SHELL=y

# Enable the mcumgr command handlers.
CONFIG_MCUMGR_CMD_IMG_MGMT=y
CONFIG_MCUMGR_CMD_OS_MGMT=y
CONFIG_MCUMGR_CMD_STAT_MGMT=y
CONFIG_MCUMGR_CMD_FS_MGMT=y

# Enable the image manager
CONFIG_IMG_MANAGER=y

# Enable file system commands
CONFIG_FILE_SYSTEM=y
CONFIG_FILE_SYSTEM_LITTLEFS=y

# Enable flash operations.
CONFIG_FLASH=y
CONFIG_FLASH_PAGE_LAYOUT=y
CONFIG_FLASH_MAP=y

# Required for file system commands
CONFIG_BASE64=y

# Some samples need a larger stack
CONFIG_SYSTEM_WORKQUEUE_STACK_SIZE=2048
CONFIG_MAIN_STACK_SIZE=2048

# Enable bootloader
CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_MCUBOOT=y

# The following configs are now valid with CONFIG_IMG_MANAGER=y
CONFIG_IMG_BLOCK_BUF_SIZE=512
CONFIG_IMG_ENABLE_IMAGE_CHECK=y

# This might still produce a warning depending on the target board and its
# configuration, but it is not a fatal error.
CONFIG_STDOUT_CONSOLE=y

# Kconfig - common architecture-specific options
#
# Copyright (c) 2017 Intel Corporation
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#

menu "Architecture-specific settings"

source "arch/$(ARCH)/Kconfig"

config FPU
	bool "Floating point services"
	default n
	depends on CPU_HAS_FPU
	help
	  This option enables the kernel's floating point services.
	  It is an overarching option that enables the other floating
	  point options below.

config FPU_SHARING
	bool "Floating point sharing"
	depends on FPU && (USERSPACE || !X86)
	help
	  This option enables the lazy context switch of floating point
	  registers. When this option is enabled, the floating point
	  registers are saved and restored only when the thread is using
	  them. This option should be enabled when multiple threads are
	  using floating point registers.

config LAZY_FP_SHARING
	bool "Lazy floating point sharing"
	depends on FPU_SHARING
	select FPU_SHARING
	help
	  This option enables the lazy context switch of floating point
	  registers. When this option is enabled, the floating point
	  registers are saved and restored only when the thread is using
	  them. This option should be enabled when multiple threads are
	  using floating point registers.

config STACK_POINTER_RANDOMIZATION
	bool "Stack pointer randomization"
	depends on !USERSPACE
	help
	  This option enables stack pointer randomization. Every time a
	  thread is scheduled, the stack pointer is moved to a random
	  offset within the thread's stack. This is a security feature
	  that makes it harder to exploit vulnerabilities related to
	  stack corruption.

config THREAD_CUSTOM_DATA
	bool "Thread custom data"
	help
	  This option enables the thread custom data feature. When this
	  option is enabled, an application can store and retrieve a
	  32-bit value in the thread object.

config THREAD_NAME
	bool "Thread names"
	help
	  This option enables the thread name feature. When this option
	  is enabled, an application can assign a name to a thread.
	  This is useful for debugging.

config THREAD_NAME_LEN
	int
	prompt "Maximum thread name length"
	default 32
	range 0 128
	depends on THREAD_NAME
	help
	  This option specifies the maximum number of characters in a thread
	  name. The value must include the null terminator.

config MAX_THREAD_BYTES
	int "Maximum bytes for thread name"
	depends on USERSPACE
	range 3 64
	default 3 if USERSPACE
	help
	  Maximum number of bytes to reserve for a thread's name.
	  Longer names will be truncated. The kernel will still
	  append a NUL terminator. A value of 3 is the minimum to
	  store at least 2 characters plus the NUL.

config ATOMIC_OPERATIONS_BUILTIN
	bool "Use built-in atomic operations"
	help
	  This option enables the use of the toolchain's built-in functions
	  for atomic operations. If this is not enabled, the architecture
	  must provide an implementation of these operations.

config HW_STACK_PROTECTION
	bool "Hardware-based stack protection"
	depends on CPU_HAS_HW_STACK_PROTECTION
	help
	  This option enables hardware-based stack protection. This is a
	  security feature that helps detect stack overflows.

config KERNEL_STACK_RESERVED_BYTES
	int "Reserved kernel stack bytes"
	default 0
	help
	  Number of bytes to reserve at the bottom of the kernel stack.
	  This is useful for architectures that need to store some data
	  at the bottom of the stack.

config BOOT_BANNER
	bool "Display boot banner"
	default y
	help
	  This option enables the display of a banner at boot time.

endmenu

/**
 * @file
 * @brief Zephyr testing framework
 *
 * This is the header for the Zephyr testing framework. This is a private header
 * and should not be included by applications.
 */

#ifndef ZEPHYR_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_TEST_H_
#define ZEPHYR_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_TEST_H_

#include <zephyr/kernel.h>
#include <zephyr/sys/iterable_sections.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

struct ztest_unit_test;

/**
 * @brief Test suite struct
 *
 * @param name Name of the test suite.
 * @param unit_tests An array of `ztest_unit_test`.
 * @param stats A pointer to a `ztest_suite_stats` struct.
 * @param pre_fn A function to be run before any of the tests in the suite are
 * run.
 * @param post_fn A function to be run after all of the tests in the suite have
 * been run.
 */
struct ztest_suite_node {
	const char *name;
	const struct ztest_unit_test *const *unit_tests;
	struct ztest_suite_stats *stats;
	ztest_handler pre_fn;
	ztest_handler post_fn;
};

/**
 * @brief A test case
 *
 * @param name Name of the test case.
 * @param test The test function.
 * @param setup The setup function.
 * @param teardown The teardown function.
 */
struct ztest_unit_test {
	const char *name;
	ztest_handler test;
	ztest_handler setup;
	ztest_handler teardown;
};

/**
 * @brief Test suite statistics
 *
 * @param fail_count The number of failed tests.
 * @param run_count The number of run tests.
 */
struct ztest_suite_stats {
	int fail_count;
	int run_count;
};

/**
 * @brief Run a test suite
 *
 * @param suite The test suite to run.
 */
void z_ztest_run_test_suite(const char *name, struct ztest_suite_node *suite);

/**
 * @brief Get the number of test suites
 *
 * @return The number of test suites.
 */
int z_ztest_get_num_test_suites(void);

/**
 * @brief A single test case, with a setup and teardown function.
 *
 * This is for the new API.
 *
 * @param fn The test function.
 * @param setup The setup function.
 * @param teardown The teardown function.
 */
#define ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(fn, setup, teardown)
	static void fn(void);
	static const struct ztest_unit_test __ztest_unit_test_##fn = {
		.name = #fn,
		.test = fn,
		.setup = setup,
		.teardown = teardown,
	};
	static void fn(void)

/**
 * @brief A single test case.
 *
 * This is for the new API.
 *
 * @param fn The test function.
 */
#define ZTEST_UNIT_TEST(fn)
	ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(fn, NULL, NULL)

/**
 * @brief A single test case, with a setup and teardown function.
 *
 * This is for the new API.
 *
 * @param fn The test function.
 * @param setup The setup function.
 * @param teardown The teardown function.
 */
#define ztest_unit_test_setup_teardown(fn, setup, teardown)
	ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(fn, setup, teardown)

/**
 * @brief Register a test suite, with pre and post functions.
 *
 * This is for the new API.
 *
 * @param suite_name The name of the test suite.
 * @param suite An array of test cases.
 * @param stats A pointer to a `ztest_suite_stats` struct.
 * @param pre The pre function.
 * @param post The post function.
 */
#define ZTEST_SUITE_REGISTRATION_PRE_POST(suite_name, suite, stats, pre, post)
	static const struct ztest_suite_node _CONCAT(__ztest_suite_node_, suite_name) = {
		.name = #suite_name,
		.unit_tests = suite,
		.stats = stats,
		.pre_fn = pre,
		.post_fn = post,
	};
	STRUCT_SECTION_ITERABLE(ztest_suite_node,
		_CONCAT(__ztest_suite_node_, suite_name))

/**
 * @brief Register a test suite.
 *
 * This is for the new API.
 *
 * @param suite_name The name of the test suite.
 * @param suite An array of test cases.
 * @param stats A pointer to a `ztest_suite_stats` struct.
 */

/*

#ifndef ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_
#define ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_

#include <zephyr/ztest.h>
#include <zephyr/sys/iterable_sections.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/**
 * @defgroup ztest_test_deprecated Ztest testing macros (deprecated)
 * @ingroup ztest
 *
 * @brief Ztest testing macros.
 *
 * @deprecated In favor of the new API, see @ref ztest_new_api.
 *
 * @{
 */

/**
 * @brief Define a test case.
 *
 * @param name The test case's name.
 * @param fn The test case's function.
 */
#define ztest_test_case(name, fn) \
	static void fn(void); \
	REGISTER_TEST_CASE(name, fn, 0)

/**
 * @brief Define a user test case.
 *
 * @param name The test case's name.
 * @param fn The test case's function.
 */
#define ztest_user_test_case(name, fn) \
	static void fn(void); \
	REGISTER_TEST_CASE(name, fn, 1)

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite.
 *
 * @param suite The test suite's name.
 * @param ... A list of `ztest_unit_test` to be included in the suite.
 */
#define ztest_test_suite(suite, ...) \
	static struct ztest_unit_test suite[] = { \
		__VA_ARGS__, \
		ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_END \
	}; \
	STRUCT_SECTION_ITERABLE(ztest_suite_node, _ztest_suite_##suite) = { \
		.name = #suite, \
		.unit_tests = suite \
	}

/**
 * @}
 */

/**
 * @defgroup ztest_new_api Ztest new testing API
 * @ingroup ztest
 *
 * @brief Ztest testing macros.
 *
 * This API is a replacement for the now deprecated @ref ztest_test_deprecated.
 *
 * @{
 */

/**
 * @brief Define a test function with setup and teardown.
 *
 * @param fn The test function's name.
 * @param setup The setup function's name.
 * @param teardown The teardown function's name.
 */
#define Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(fn, setup, teardown) \
	{ \
		.name = #fn, \
		.test = fn, \
		.setup = setup, \
		.teardown = teardown, \
	}

/**
 * @brief Define a test function.
 *
 * @param fn The test function's name.
 */
#define ztest_unit_test(fn) \
	Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(fn, NULL, NULL)

/**
 * @brief Define a test function with a setup function.
 *
 * @param fn The test function's name.
 * @param setup The setup function's name.
 */
#define ztest_unit_test_setup(fn, setup) \
	Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(fn, setup, NULL)

/**
 * @brief Define a test function with a teardown function.
 *
 * @param fn The test function's name.
 * @param teardown The teardown function's name.
 */
#define ztest_unit_test_teardown(fn, teardown) \
	Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(fn, NULL, teardown)

/**
 * @brief Define a test function with setup and teardown functions.
 *
 * @param fn The test function's name.
 * @param setup The setup function's name.
 * @param teardown The teardown function's name.
 */
#define ztest_unit_test_setup_teardown(fn, setup, teardown) \
	Z_ZTEST_UNIT_TEST_SETUP_TEARDOWN(fn, setup, teardown)

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite with setup and teardown.
 *
 * @internal
 *
 * @param suite The test suite's name.
 * @param setup The setup function's name.
 * @param teardown The teardown function's name.
 * @param ... A list of `ztest_unit_test` to be included in the suite.
 */
#define Z_ZTEST_TEST_SUITE_DEFINE(suite, setup, teardown, ...) \
	static struct ztest_unit_test _ztest_unit_test_##suite[] = { \
		__VA_ARGS__ \
	}; \
	STRUCT_SECTION_ITERABLE(ztest_suite_node, _ztest_suite_##suite) = { \
		.name = #suite, \
		.unit_tests = _ztest_unit_test_##suite, \
		.count = ARRAY_SIZE(_ztest_unit_test_##suite), \
		.setup = setup, \
		.teardown = teardown, \
	}

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite.
 *
 * @param suite The test suite's name.
 * @param ... A list of `ztest_unit_test` to be included in the suite.
 */
#define ztest_new_test_suite(suite, ...) \
	Z_ZTEST_TEST_SUITE_DEFINE(suite, NULL, NULL, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite with setup and teardown functions.
 *
 * @param suite The test suite's name.
 * @param setup The setup function's name.
 * @param teardown The teardown function's name.
 * @param ... A list of `ztest_unit_test` to be included in the suite.
 */
#define ztest_test_suite_with_setup_teardown(suite, setup, teardown, ...) \
	Z_ZTEST_TEST_SUITE_DEFINE(suite, setup, teardown, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Define a simple asynchronous test function.
 *
 * This macro is used to define a simple asynchronous test function that uses a single
 * k_sem to signal completion.
 *
 * @param fn The test function's name.
 */
#define ztest_simple_async_test(fn) \
	static K_SEM_DEFINE(async_sem, 0, 1); \
	static void fn(void *data)

/**
 * @brief End a simple asynchronous test function.
 *
 * This macro is used to end a simple asynchronous test function and wait for the
 * completion signal.
 */
#define ztest_async_test_end() \
	k_sem_take(&async_sem, K_FOREVER)

/**
 * @brief Signal completion of a simple asynchronous test function.
 *
 * This macro is used to signal the completion of a simple asynchronous test function.
 */
#define ztest_async_test_signal() \
	k_sem_give(&async_sem)

/**
 * @}
 */

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_ */

#ifndef ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_
#define ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_

#include <zephyr/ztest.h>
#include <zephyr/sys/iterable_sections.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/**
 * @brief Test suite structure.
 */
struct ztest_suite {
	const char *name;
	/** Predicate function to be run before the test suite is run */
	bool (*predicate)(const void *data);
	/** Test suite setup function */
	void (*setup)(void *data);
	/** Test suite teardown function */
	void (*teardown)(void *data);
	/** Test case setup function */
	void (*before)(void *data);
	/** Test case teardown function */
	void (*after)(void *data);
	/** Pointer to the array of test cases */
	struct ztest_unit_test *unit_tests;
	/** User data to be passed to the test suite functions */
	void *user_data;
};

#if defined(CONFIG_ZTEST_SHUFFLE)
#define ZTEST_SHUFFLE_SECTION K_SHUFFLE_SECTION
#else
#define ZTEST_SHUFFLE_SECTION
#endif

/**
 * @internal
 * @brief Define a test suite.
 *
 * This is the internal macro that is used to define a test suite. It is not
 * meant to be used directly by users.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param predicate The predicate function to be run before the test suite is run.
 * @param setup The test suite setup function.
 * @param teardown The test suite teardown function.
 * @param before The test case setup function.
 * @param after The test case teardown function.
 * @param user_data The user data to be passed to the test suite functions.
 * @param ... A list of @ref ztest_unit_test calls.
 */
#define ZTEST_SUITE_DEFINE(suite, predicate, setup, teardown, before, after, user_data, ...) \
	static struct ztest_unit_test suite##_tests[] ZTEST_SHUFFLE_SECTION = { \
		__VA_ARGS__ \
		ZTEST_UNIT_TEST(ztest_test_pass) /* Array terminator */ \
	}; \
	STRUCT_SECTION_ITERABLE(ztest_suite, suite##_suite) = { \
		.name = #suite, \
		.predicate = predicate, \
		.unit_tests = suite##_tests, \
		.setup = setup, \
		.teardown = teardown, \
		.before = before, \
		.after = after, \
		.user_data = user_data, \
	}

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite with setup and teardown functions.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param setup The test suite setup function.
 * @param teardown The test suite teardown function.
 * @param ... A list of @ref ztest_unit_test calls.
 */
#define ztest_test_suite_pre_post(suite, setup, teardown, ...) \
	ZTEST_SUITE_DEFINE(suite, NULL, setup, teardown, NULL, NULL, NULL, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite with a setup function.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param setup The test suite setup function.
 * @param ... A list of @ref ztest_unit_test calls.
 */
#define ztest_test_suite_pre(suite, setup, ...) \
	ZTEST_SUITE_DEFINE(suite, NULL, setup, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite with a teardown function.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param teardown The test suite teardown function.
 * @param ... A list of @ref ztest_unit_test calls.
 */
#define ztest_test_suite_post(suite, teardown, ...) \
	ZTEST_SUITE_DEFINE(suite, NULL, NULL, teardown, NULL, NULL, NULL, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite with user data.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param user_data The user data to be passed to the test suite functions.
 * @param predicate The predicate function to be run before the test suite is run.
 * @param setup The test suite setup function.
 * @param before The test case setup function.
 * @param after The test case teardown function.
 * @param teardown The test suite teardown function.
 * @param ... A list of @ref ztest_unit_test calls.
 */
#define ztest_test_suite_with_user_data(suite, user_data, predicate, setup, before, after, \
					teardown, ...) \
	ZTEST_SUITE_DEFINE(suite, predicate, setup, teardown, before, after, user_data, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Define a test suite.
 *
 * @param suite The name of the test suite.
 * @param ... A list of @ref ztest_unit_test calls.
 */
#define ztest_test_suite(suite, ...) \
	ZTEST_SUITE_DEFINE(suite, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Get a test suite by name.
 *
 * @param suite_name The name of the test suite to get.
 *
 * @return A pointer to the test suite, or NULL if not found.
 */
struct ztest_suite *ztest_get_test_suite_by_name(const char *suite_name);

/**
 * @brief Run a test suite by name.
 *
 * @param suite_name The name of the test suite to run.
 *
 * @return The number of failed tests.
 */
int ztest_run_test_suite_by_name(const char *suite_name);

/**
 * @brief Run a test suite.
 *
 * @param suite The test suite to run.
 *
 * @return The number of failed tests.
 */
#define ztest_run_test_suite(suite) \
	ztest_run_test_suite_by_name(STRINGIFY(suite))

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* ZEPHYR_SUBSYS_TESTSUITE_ZTEST_INCLUDE_ZTEST_TEST_H_ */

/*
